definition: A race-notice statute is a type of recording act which gives priority of title to the first bona fide purchaser to record their claim. For example: A purchases a plot of land from O. The next day, B also purchases that plot of land from O. B records their claim before A. Under a race-notice statute, B’s claim has priority over A’s claim if and only if B was a bona fide purchaser, meaning B had no actual or constructive notice as to A’s claim.
